structure.source: NIST CCCBDB experimental geometry, reference 1973Dun/McK (r C–H 1.090 Å, r C–Cl 1.785 Å, Cartesian 1.7854 Å; angle H–C–H 110.75°)

notes.title: Inequivalent ligands
notes.text: Three hydrogens and one chlorine: fix-and-flip pairing applies only within the set of three hydrogens, and the counting bond order assumes equivalent bonds, which these are not. The density-matrix bond orders, shown per bond, are the better guide here (spec section 3, flagged but drawn).

notes.title: σ only for chlorine
notes.text: Chlorine contributes one inward-pointing 3p σ orbital; its other 3p orbitals (lone pairs) are left out. The C–Cl coupling comes from the universal Harrison law (CONVENTIONS v1.6), as every coupling does.
